quizzes.stem: Scenario: Priya compares four designs for a call-centre assistant. Two of them meet every service level, one at 90,000 a month and one at 140,000. A third costs 40,000 but misses the latency target. Which does the record recommend?

options.a: The cheaper of the two that qualify, since price decides among them
options.b: The 140,000 design, because the larger budget leaves room to grow beyond the target
options.c: The 40,000 design, because it is the cheapest of the four and the target can be tuned later
options.d: Both of the designs that meet every level, so that the sponsor can pick the one preferred

explanation.a: A design must qualify first, and among those that do, the cheapest is recommended.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "An option that misses a service level is not a candidate, however cheap".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the newest" and "the most capable" are not criteria, as "the cheapest one that meets the service levels" is.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Two recommended options push the choice back to the reader".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Hugo must brief a sponsor who will decide in one meeting on whether a pilot goes ahead. Hugo's draft is six pages of tables, ending with the break-even derivation. What should the first page of the record hold?

options.a: The derivation of the break-even, which is the reason for every later number
options.b: The table by segment, so the sponsor sees the accuracy figures before anything else
options.c: A short summary in plain words, covering the cost, the risk and the decision requested
options.d: The list of the model's settings, so the sponsor can confirm the configuration

explanation.c: The sponsor stops reading early, so the summary comes first and ends in the decision.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the table by segment belongs with "the numbers that produced it" for the engineer.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The summary is first because the sponsor stops reading early".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the sponsor's summary has "no percentages of percentages, no model names".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Ola's team reports its latency service level, a ceiling of 2000 ms at the 95th percentile. The week's measured figure is exactly 2000 ms. How does the report read?

options.a: Missed by 0 ms, since the measure has reached the limit
options.b: Met, since a value at the limit counts as inside it
options.c: Met, but with the ceiling raised to 2100 ms for the week
options.d: Undecided until a second week of measurements arrives

explanation.b: A service level is met at its limit exactly.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A latency of 2000 ms against a ceiling of 2000 ms is met".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the ceiling is the target, and "Met at the limit exactly" leaves no reason to raise it.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Met at the limit exactly" settles the case without a second week.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Vera is writing the pilot table for a billing assistant and offers the stop trigger "if the quality is worse than we hoped". What is wrong with it?

options.a: It should name the reviewer who decides when quality is poor enough
options.b: It states a quality aim, which belongs to the sponsor and not the pilot
options.c: It should come after the roll-out so that the data exists to judge it
options.d: It holds no number, so reaching it is a matter of opinion

explanation.d: A trigger needs a number to be reached.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A trigger that says \"if it goes wrong\" is not a trigger", whoever decides.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the record lists each assumption "with a test and a stop trigger that has a number in it" before the pilot runs.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the stop trigger is the pilot's own", so the aim may be the sponsor's while the trigger is not.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Noor tells a sponsor that an assistant is "98 percent accurate overall". The system answers three kinds of dispute, and the one that costs 250 per error is right 63 times in 100. What should the record say to the sponsor?

options.a: That the costly kind is excluded from the figure because it is handled in another system
options.b: That the overall figure stands, since the costly kind is a small share of the traffic
options.c: That a person decides each of those until the measured result improves
options.d: That the figure will be re-measured once per quarter, with the same overall method

explanation.c: The promise is made per segment, and a person decides the costly one.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "an average hides the segments that cost the most", whatever the traffic share.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says to "Promise what you measure and measure what you promise", and excluding a segment breaks both.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a promise is made once and kept for as long as the system runs", so re-measuring the same overall figure repeats the same blind spot.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Lars hands a finished assistant to an operations team with an architecture diagram and a list of settings. The first alert fires on a Saturday and nobody knows who should act on it. Which part of the hand-off was missing?

options.a: A longer pilot, so that more alerts would have fired before the launch
options.b: A named owner for the service and a runbook that tells staff what to do
options.c: A monthly report to the sponsor listing the alerts of the previous period
options.d: A second diagram showing the alert thresholds drawn on the architecture

explanation.b: The record names an owner and a runbook for each alert.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a diagram without the runbook leaves the first incident to the person who happens to remember", and a longer pilot adds no owner.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The people who run the system are not the people who built it", and a report to the sponsor does not reach them on a Saturday.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Implementation guidance is part of the hand-off and not an extra", and a second diagram adds none.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: A reviewer corrects forty answers in a week, and the notes of the sponsor review record them. Nothing else changes, and the same errors appear the next week. Which step would have closed the loop?

options.a: Sending the notes to the engineers with a request to read them before the next release
options.b: Asking the reviewers to correct the same answers a second time for the record
options.c: Moving the review from weekly to daily so that the notes are fresher
options.d: Turning each fix into a labelled evaluation case that each later release is run against

explanation.d: A loop is closed when a change goes back out through the gate.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A stakeholder review that produces notes and no cases has not closed anything".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the review is "A regular review of the segments, the saving and the open risks", and its speed adds no case.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a loop closes only when "the person who raised the problem is told what happened" after a change has gone through the gate.
